experiment: Two-original-model model+native-recipe pilot, not a pure architecture causal ablation
source: Original publisher checkpoints, fresh zero-B q/v LoRA; no F22 adapter loaded

inference.primary: Same command-only ngram8 guard for both baselines and both SFT models
inference.raw_diagnostic: DEV32 baseline and final only, no guard; no checkpoint selection using raw outputs

metrics: v6 behavioral PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN on DEV32 and TRAINprobe32
Old64 native partial score, strict total and baseline-correct retained/lost
actual training time, generation tokens and GPU memory
decision: Report fixed final256 plus intermediate128 for every model; no best-checkpoint selection, no model promotion. Do not change recipes based on outputs. Stop each arm at256 updates even if scores are poor.
fairness: Same sample exposure/update order and nominal LoRA hyperparameters; tokenizers and format differ, so not equal token/FLOP budget. Compare improvement relative to each model own paired baseline. One seed only.
gpu: One GPU at a time; same GPU product for both model arms; <=4 allocated hours total for new model pilot, no priority/toleration bypass
validation: V6 Linux oracle controls and uniform old-output review must pass before submitting GPU job. Input/source hashes, labels, real gradients, weight export/reload must be verified.

redsage.format: Unchanged RedSage inference prefill plus explicitly declared BPE empty-think completion intervention

qwen.format: Official Qwen native non-thinking prompt; direct output completion; no RedSage BPE patch

oracle_method: v6: actual dry-run must report expected aggregate links and preserve all files; separate disposable shadow fixture removes only explicit dry-run flag and verifies intended link partition. This is evaluator verification, not a model-authored real execution.
pending_conflict: An already-authorized owned GPU task from another conversation is observed without cancellation; this pilot waits to avoid duplicate GPU usage.
